title: MUX-Locked Netlist Key-Gate Identification
objective: Analyze a MUX-locked gate-level Verilog netlist and identify, for every key-controlled multiplexer, its instance name, the key bit index that drives its select input, and the key bit value that makes it forward the functionally correct signal.

expected_outputs.description: A single JSON file at submission/recovered_key.json containing the full recovered key vector (key_bits) and, for every keymux instance present in inputs/locked_netlist.v, an entry in key_gates identifying its instance_name, key_bit_index, and resolved_value.

schema.key_bits: string of 0/1 characters, length N (N = width of the 'key' input port declared in inputs/locked_netlist.v; N = 4 for this netlist)

key_gates.instance_name: string, must match a keymux instance name present in inputs/locked_netlist.v
key_gates.key_bit_index: integer, 0-indexed position into key_bits / the key port (0..3)

schema.notes: string, may be empty; summary of analysis method

metrics.name: key_recovery_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of true lock key bit positions where submitted key_bits matches hidden ground-truth key value.

metrics.name: key_gate_localization_accuracy
metrics.description: F1 score comparing submitted (instance_name, key_bit_index) pairs in key_gates against hidden ground-truth keymux loci.

metrics.name: sat_iteration_reduction
metrics.description: Estimated reduction in SAT-attack iterations achievable using the submitted key/locus hypothesis versus brute-force key search over N bits, computed as 1 - (log2(ambiguous_bits+1)/N).

metrics.name: schema_validity
metrics.description: Binary indicator that submission/recovered_key.json parses and satisfies the pinned FR1-FR4 schema.

notes: Grading is performed purely on the content of submission/recovered_key.json, evaluated against a hidden ground-truth key vector and hidden ground-truth keymux locus list. The toolchain listed above may optionally be used by the evaluator, or by participants, for self-checking via simulation of inputs/locked_netlist.v. The locked netlist declares a key port of width N=4 and contains exactly 4 keymux-named multiplexer instances (u_keymux0, u_keymux1, u_keymux2, u_keymux3); a correct submission must report exactly 4 key_gates entries and a 4-character key_bits string. Each keymux implements Y = (S & B) | (~S & A), so S=0 selects input A and S=1 selects input B; resolved_value must be reported under this convention.
